Suppose $\log(a)=m$ and $\log(b)=n$. That means $10^m=a$ and $10^n=b$.

$\begin{align}
\maroonE{a} \cdot \goldE{b} &= \maroonE{10^m} \cdot \goldE{10^n} &\text{Substitute.}\\\\
a \cdot b &=10^{m+n}&\text{Product property}\\\\
10^{\log(a\cdot b)} &=10^{m+n}&\text{Inverse relationship}\\\\
\log(a \cdot b) &= \redE{m} + \purpleD{n}&\text{Equate the exponents.}\\\\
\log(a \cdot b) &= \redE{\log(a)} + \purpleD{\log(b)}&\text{Substitute.}
\end{align}$
